study type: secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial
exposure: Subcuticular suture for skin closure after cesarean delivery
Metallic staples for skin closure after cesarean delivery
outcome: Wound complication occurring after hospital discharge (infection, wound disruption, seroma, hematoma)
cohort: 350 women undergoing cesarean delivery at >=24 weeks' gestation were randomized to receive metallic staples or subcuticular suture for skin closure.
finding: After multivariable adjustment, the type of skin closure method (suture vs. staples) was not associated with wound complications occurring after hospital discharge following cesarean delivery.
